items.title: California's Filing Deadline
items.desc: Most injury claims in California must be filed within two years, but claims against a government entity can require notice in as little as six months. Waiting too long can close the door on your case.

items.title: Fault Doesn't Have to Be Clear-Cut
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, so you can still recover damages even if you were partly responsible for the accident. Your compensation is simply reduced by your share of fault, not eliminated.

items.title: No Cap on Pain and Suffering
items.desc: In ordinary injury cases, California places no limit on non-economic damages like pain and suffering. That means your recovery isn't artificially capped by state law.

items.title: No Upfront Cost to You
items.desc: Attorneys in our network work on contingency, so they only get paid if you recover money. That removes the financial barrier to getting legal advice after an accident.

items.question: How long do I have to file an injury claim in California?
items.answer: Generally, you have two years from the date of the accident to file a personal injury claim in California. If a government entity was involved, the window can be much shorter, sometimes as little as six months to file a claim notice. It's wise not to wait, since evidence and witness memory can fade quickly.

items.question: Can I still recover money if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: Yes. California uses a pure comparative fault system, which means your compensation is reduced by your percentage of fault rather than denied outright. Even if you were 40% or 60% responsible, you may still be able to recover the remaining share.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to happen in San Juan Bautista?
items.answer: Public crash records show that reported collisions in San Juan Bautista cluster along corridors like Rt 156, The Alameda Road, and SR-156, including its westbound stretch. These are simply the roads with the highest recorded collision counts, not a judgment about safety. Timing-wise, reports have tended to peak on Sundays between 6 and 8 p.m.

items.question: Is there a limit on how much I can recover for pain and suffering?
items.answer: No. California does not cap non-economic damages, such as pain and suffering, in ordinary personal injury cases. This differs from some other states and can matter significantly depending on the nature of your injuries.
